questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: If you are riding alongside another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit and then exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is unsafe. You could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The vehicle may also block your escape route if danger appears. Speed up or drop back to get away from this position.

questions.question: Which of these provides the best face protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield that does not shatter protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: When are motorcyclists safest?

options.text: On the side of the road.
In the left side of the lane.

questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are safest when other drivers can clearly see them. Use your headlight, brake light, signals, and good lane position to be more visible.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when riding near stopped or slow-moving cars?

options.text: Pull over and wait until traffic begins to move.
Ride on the shoulder to get through the area as quickly as possible.
Weave between the cars to get through the area as quickly as possible.

questions.explanation: Weaving between stopped or parked cars is dangerous. Car doors may open or cars may pull into traffic suddenly. You will not have room to escape. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
Coming to a complete stop before you expect to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you can lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: What should a good lane position do?

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Communicate your intentions to other road users.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards on the road. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. These signs tell you the traffic rules. You must follow them.

questions.question: Can one alcoholic drink affect your riding?

options.text: Judgment and riding abilities can still be affected.
There is usually no effect on the body.
There is an effect on the body, but it only lasts for a short time.
There is an effect on the body, but it can be eliminated by drinking coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and riding abilities can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your judgment and riding skills. Your body needs time to remove alcohol. Coffee cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night compared to during the day, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Allow more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.explanation: To stay safe when riding at night, slow down and increase the distance between you and other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Always be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check your motorcycle. What do you NOT need to check?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, grip the handlebars firmly. Slow down by easing off the throttle and going straight. If you need to brake, gently apply the brake on the good tire. Move toward the road edge as you slow down, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Do not signal, as it may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing a vehicle on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal your intentions and check for traffic. Pass only when it is safe, then signal and return to your original lane when you can.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
Your entire face, including your eyes.
Your face less well than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire face, including your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to weave while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is usually not dangerous. Stay calm and go straight ahead at a steady speed. Trying to zigzag will make it more dangerous.

questions.question: Which of these will protect your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not protect your eyes well enough.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of serious injury in a crash, what should you NOT rely on?
questions.explanation: To reduce injury risk, wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar when you accelerate?

options.text: It feels like it is falling behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. Because of its weight, it will feel like it is falling behind when you speed up.

questions.question: When securing a load on your motorcycle, where should you place it?

options.text: On only one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Place loads as low as possible. Placing them too high, such as on a sissy bar, can raise the center of gravity and affect balance. Distribute loads evenly on both sides to avoid pulling the motorcycle to one side.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers see you if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Focus on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still don't see them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Don't use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, make yourself visible, tell others what you plan to do, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react quickly.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo, what happens?

options.text: It takes less time to speed up, but more time to stop.
It takes more time to speed up and stop.
It takes more time to speed up, but less time to stop.
It takes less time to speed up and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to speed up and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from cargo or a passenger makes your motorcycle slower to speed up and slower to stop compared to riding alone.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: ______ guarantees that another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. It is safest to assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will.
